question: Should Gateway support scheme-level browser-origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should that live inside `allowedOrigins` or in a dedicated constrained pattern setting?
rationale: This changes which browser-origin WebSocket and trusted-proxy HTTP requests may pass Gateway authorization, so automation should not choose the wildcard grammar or security posture on its own.

options.title: Define constrained pattern contract
options.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension/custom-scheme cases before implementation.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Land an exact opaque-origin fix separately and defer changing-extension-ID wildcard support as outside current Gateway policy.

options.title: Allow only Chrome extension scheme wildcard
options.body: Support `chrome-extension://*` narrowly with scheme-specific matching and negative security tests rather than generic prefix wildcards.

recommendation.title: Define constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed pattern grammar, docs, audit handling, and allow/reject tests for approved extension/custom-scheme cases before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and evolved the Gateway origin-security boundary most directly affected by this decision.
